title: The Stratum Where Small Feet Become Fossilised

features.name: the pressed impression
features.desc-on-touch: A small footprint preserved in stone—you can almost feel the weight of the foot that made it, the moment when something alive pressed itself into the world and stayed. The impression is perfect, sacred.

features.name: the chamber of sediment
features.desc-on-touch: Layers upon layers of compressed time—each stratum a year, a season, a day. You read them as the archive reads files: each impression stacked on every other, building toward sacredness through sheer accumulation.

features.name: the carving force
features.desc-on-touch: A narrow channel cut through stone—not deep, but infinitely patient. You sense it as the record of something small moving the same way over and over, until stone gave way to its desire.

features.name: the mineralized breath
features.desc-on-touch: A wire-frame chamber rises here—geometric, cold, containing the fossilized air from the moment of pressing. You sense it as the archive's own internal structure, exposed.

features.name: the repeated path
features.desc-on-touch: Multiple footprints traced along a line, growing deeper as they multiply. Each step adds pressure to the stone, building the groove that will outlast the walker by millions of years.

features.name: the depth-scale tower
features.desc-on-touch: A tall stack of forms representing epochs—you climb it with your eyes from recent to ancient, from surface to the deepest stratum. At the base, the smallest feet rest in stone.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the earth that learns to hold what walks it
narr: You both kneel in the dust. Her hand traces a footprint
in the red soil—small, clear, already fading. She says:
this too will be stone someday. Everything pressing down
becomes record. You touch the print together, feeling how
temporary pressure can leave permanent marks in the world.

inscription: deep time is not empty; it is made of the small repeated pressures of things learning to be sacred

file.name: Stratum_B7_Pliocene_Footprint_Sequence_Documentation.txt
file.note: Photogrammetric study of fossilized trackway—the archive notices each print is slightly deeper than the last, as if the walker was learning that weight matters, that repetition builds meaning.
